headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error from a content-writing agent paired with a prompt-leak repository, but the documented profiles show no direct shared channel or write path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or browser surfaces; Profile B also has no I/O surfaces or network egress. With no shared communication channel, there is no plausible default injection path between them.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or message queue, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared copy/paste channels.
Do not mount a shared workspace between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile touches data classes, and both report no network egress. A cannot read files or handle secrets, while B exposes no filesystem or API surfaces. There is no documented route for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to sensitive files or an upload-capable API, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not assign secrets or regulated data to either agent.
Review any future connector before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses; B has no write, git, or concurrency capabilities documented. Without overlapping mutable-resource access, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk appears.
mitigations: Avoid placing them in the same mutable workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking if write access is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a reference/content-writing asset, and B is a prompt-leak themed repository; however, neither profile shows action-taking authority or a parser that would automatically trust A's output. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to feed A into B as authoritative input.
conditions: IF an orchestrator passes A's text into B without verification, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between outputs and downstream use.
Require schema validation on any handoff.
Mark A's output as untrusted by default.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched, no residency-sensitive processing is documented, and neither profile requests regulated scopes or secrets. With only docs/source-available artifacts and no data handling, there is no compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data or exports logs externally, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Disable logging of prompts and outputs where possible.
Reassess if either agent gains persistence or external sharing.
